question.prompt: When \(x=2\), find the value of \(\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)\cdot x\).

solutions.explanation: First calculate inside the parentheses: \(1+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{2}\). Then multiply by \(2\) to get \(3\).
solutions.title: Substitute and calculate

solutions.explanation:
Distributing the factor \(x\) makes the reciprocal product equal to \(1\). Since \(x=2\ne0\),
\[
\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)x=x+\frac{1}{x}\cdot x=x+1.
\]
At \(x=2\), the value is \(2+1=3\).
solutions.title: Use the distributive law
